blocks.content: 1. Excretion – Concept and Importance

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Excretion is essential for maintaining homeostasis, ionic balance, and fluid pH.
The nephron is the fundamental structural and functional unit of the kidney.
Urine formation comprises three primary processes: ultrafiltration, selective reabsorption, and tubular secretion.
Hormones such as ADH and Aldosterone strictly regulate water and sodium reabsorption.
Kidney failure can be managed artificially using dialysis or permanently treated via kidney transplant.

blocks.content:
Excretion is the biological process by which metabolic waste products are removed from the body.
During metabolism, harmful substances such as carbon dioxide, urea, uric acid, excess salts, and water are produced.
If these wastes accumulate, they can disturb normal body functions and may lead to toxicity.
Excretion helps in maintaining a stable internal environment, known as homeostasis.
It also helps in regulating osmotic balance, ionic balance, and pH of body fluids.
Thus, excretion is essential for survival of all living organisms.
2. Nitrogenous Wastes

Nitrogenous wastes are produced due to breakdown of proteins and nucleic acids.
The three main nitrogenous wastes are ammonia, urea, and uric acid.
Ammonia is highly toxic and is excreted by aquatic animals.
Urea is less toxic and is excreted by mammals.
Uric acid is least toxic and is excreted by birds and reptiles.
Humans are ureotelic organisms as they excrete urea.
Type of waste depends on habitat and water availability.
3. Human Excretory System – Organs

The human excretory system consists of a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra.
Kidneys filter blood and form urine.
Ureters transport urine from kidneys to urinary bladder.
Urinary bladder temporarily stores urine.
Urethra helps in elimination of urine from the body.
Together, these organs ensure efficient waste removal.
4. Kidney – External Structure

Kidneys are reddish-brown, bean-shaped organs.
They are located on either side of the vertebral column in the abdominal cavity.
The right kidney is slightly lower due to the presence of liver.
Each kidney is surrounded by a protective layer of fat.
Renal artery brings blood to the kidney and renal vein carries filtered blood away.
5. Kidney – Internal Structure

Internally, each kidney has three regions: cortex, medulla, and renal pelvis.
The cortex is the outer granular region.
The medulla is the inner striated region containing renal pyramids.
Renal pelvis is a funnel-shaped structure that collects urine.
Urine from pelvis passes into ureter.
Structural organization helps in efficient urine formation.
6. Nephron – Functional Unit of Kidney

Nephron is the structural and functional unit of kidney.
Each kidney has about one million nephrons.
A nephron consists of renal corpuscle and renal tubule.
Renal corpuscle includes glomerulus and Bowman’s capsule.
Renal tubule includes PCT, loop of Henle, and DCT.
Nephrons perform filtration, reabsorption, and secretion.
Excretion is the biological process by which metabolic waste products are removed from the body.
7. Blood Supply to Nephron

Blood enters nephron through afferent arteriole.
It leaves through efferent arteriole.
The glomerulus is a network of capillaries where filtration occurs.
High blood pressure in glomerulus helps in ultrafiltration.
Peritubular capillaries surround renal tubule.
They help in reabsorption of substances.
8. Formation of Urine – Ultrafiltration

Ultrafiltration occurs in the glomerulus.
Blood is filtered due to high pressure.
Water, glucose, amino acids, urea, and salts enter Bowman’s capsule.
Blood cells and plasma proteins remain in blood.
The filtrate formed is called glomerular filtrate.
This is the first step of urine formation.
9. Reabsorption

Reabsorption occurs mainly in the proximal convoluted tubule.
Useful substances like glucose, amino acids, sodium ions, and water are reabsorbed.
Reabsorption prevents loss of essential substances.
Some reabsorption also occurs in loop of Henle and DCT.
This step helps in conserving nutrients and water.
10. Tubular Secretion

Tubular secretion occurs mainly in distal convoluted tubule.
Excess ions like potassium and hydrogen ions are secreted.
Certain drugs and wastes are also added to urine.
This process helps in maintaining ionic and acid-base balance.
Tubular secretion completes urine formation.
11. Role of Loop of Henle

Loop of Henle plays a crucial role in concentrating urine.
It creates a concentration gradient in the medulla.
Descending limb allows water reabsorption.
Ascending limb allows salt reabsorption.
This mechanism helps conserve water in the body.
12. Hormonal Regulation of Excretion

Hormones regulate water and salt balance.
ADH increases water reabsorption in collecting ducts.
Aldosterone increases sodium reabsorption.
Atrial natriuretic peptide decreases sodium reabsorption.
Hormonal imbalance can cause abnormal urine output.
13. Urinary Bladder and Micturition

Urinary bladder is a muscular sac that stores urine.
Stretch receptors signal when bladder is full.
Micturition is the process of urine release.
It is controlled by nervous system.
In adults, urination can be controlled voluntarily.
14. Excretion in Other Organisms

Different organisms show different modes of excretion.
Amoeba excretes by diffusion.
Earthworm uses nephridia.
Insects use Malpighian tubules.
Plants remove wastes through stomata and shedding leaves.
This shows diversity in excretory mechanisms.

items: Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) is the primary site for selective reabsorption.
The right kidney is positioned lower than the left kidney due to the space occupied by the liver.
The Loop of Henle is crucial for concentrating urine by establishing a concentration gradient in the medulla.
Humans are classified as ureotelic because they excrete nitrogenous waste primarily as urea.

blocks.content: 15. Disorders of Excretory System

Kidney stones are formed by crystallization of calcium salts.
Nephritis is inflammation of kidney.
Uremia is accumulation of urea in blood.
Renal failure occurs when kidneys stop functioning.
Early diagnosis is important to prevent damage.
16. Dialysis and Kidney Transplant

Dialysis is artificial purification of blood.
It is used in kidney failure.
Hemodialysis uses a dialysis machine.
Peritoneal dialysis uses peritoneum as membrane.
Kidney transplant is permanent treatment.
Donor kidney replaces non-functioning kidney.
17. IMPORTANT FACTS – SSC FOCUS

• Humans are ureotelic.
• Nephron is functional unit of kidney.
• Ultrafiltration occurs in glomerulus.
• PCT is major site of reabsorption.
• Loop of Henle concentrates urine.
• ADH regulates water balance.
• Aldosterone regulates sodium balance.
• Renal failure treated by dialysis.
• Kidney transplant is permanent solution.
• Right kidney lies lower than left.
